title: Yash Addresses Toxic Delays, Shelving Rumors Ahead of August 26 Release
excerpt: At the Bengaluru trailer launch of Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups, the KGF star hit back at persistent rumors about the film being abandoned, revealing a grueling 200-day shoot and calling it 'an Indian film' that transcends regional boundaries.
body:
• Yash addressed shelving rumors at the Toxic trailer launch in Bengaluru on August 8, calling the reports baseless and revealing the film was shot over 200 days.
  • Toxic was originally set for a March 19 clash with Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2 but was postponed twice — first to June 4 (citing Middle East tensions), then to its current August 26 release date.
  • The film, directed by Geetu Mohandas and budgeted at Rs 850–1,000 crore, stars Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, and Rukmini Vasanth alongside Yash.
  • Yash described Toxic as a pan-Indian project filmed in Kannada and English, positioning it as a departure from the KGF franchise and a step toward global Indian cinema.

Yash Fires Back at Shelving Rumors

At a packed trailer launch event in Bengaluru on August 8, Kannada superstar Yash broke his silence on the persistent rumors that had swirled around Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups for months — including reports that the film had been shelved entirely.

https://x.com/kunalreviewer/status/2089270861585064169

"Every 10th day or 20th day, there will be news about a film being shelved, a film being stopped. I don't know from where they write these stories."

— Yash, at the Toxic trailer launch in Bengaluru

The actor explained that a production of Toxic's scale was bound to involve logistical challenges, with the team coordinating numerous actors, locations, and schedules across a 200-day shoot that began on August 8, 2024 — exactly two years before the trailer unveiling. "Making a film is like going to war against the whole world," Yash said, adding that his producer Venkat K Narayana "stood like a rock" throughout.

From March Clash to August Solo Release

Toxic's journey to theatres has been anything but straightforward. The film was originally slated for March 19, 2026, putting it in direct competition with Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar: The Revenge — a clash that had trade analysts and exhibitors on edge.

In early March, the makers pushed the release to June 4, citing the escalating conflict in the Middle East and its impact on Gulf cinema markets. An official statement from KVN Productions and Monster Mind Creations noted that the Gulf region, handled by distributor Phars Films, was a "crucial territory" for the multi-language release.

A source close to the production told Bollywood Hungama at the time: "Yash loved Dhurandhar and is looking forward to Part 2. All the rivalry, anxiety and competitiveness is created by outsiders." The source added that the move was driven by business considerations in the Gulf, not fear of competition.

The June date did not hold either. In late April, Yash issued a second postponement statement, saying the team needed more time to ensure the film "reaches the world with the impact it is meant to have." The release is now confirmed for August 26, 2026.

A Pan-Indian Ambition

Yash positioned Toxic as a film that transcends regional cinema boundaries. "Now it is no more Kannada, Tamil, Telugu. This is an Indian film," he said at the trailer launch. "This movie is not just a Kannada film; this is an Indian film where all the top stars, all the successful people, and all the talented people have contributed."

Shot in both Kannada and English, Toxic will also release in dubbed versions in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam. The ensemble cast includes Nayanthara, Kiara Advani, Huma Qureshi, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth, Akshay Oberoi, and Sudev Nair.

Yash acknowledged that assembling so many established names brought its own challenges. "This film has happened because all these lovely, talented, successful people have kept their egos aside, kept other things aside, and they've just come with one cause, to put Indian film on a global platform," he said.

Geetu Mohandas and a Departure from KGF

Directed by Geetu Mohandas, Toxic is set against the backdrop of post-colonial Goa and follows Raya (Yash) as he builds his own criminal empire. With a reported budget of Rs 850–1,000 crore, it is one of the most expensive Indian films ever produced.

Yash was candid about the film not being a conventional crowd-pleaser. "This movie is a very tough one because the kind of decisions, on the surface level, it was not easy. It is not a perfect commercial package film," he said.

"I always believe in directors' passion than their past success. She had a burning passion, desire, and wanted to show the world what she is capable of doing and what true cinema can be."

— Yash, on director Geetu Mohandas

Earlier, at CinemaCon, Yash had defended the film's sensual promotional material against "obscene" criticisms, calling a "gangster film with a female gaze" something "very new and refreshing" for Indian cinema.

What's Next

Toxic is now set for a worldwide theatrical release on August 26, 2026. Veteran trade analyst Taran Adarsh had earlier called the March postponement a "wise call," noting that Yash "enjoys tremendous fan following in the Middle East" and that skipping the Gulf market would have meant "a loss of a big chunk of revenue" for the high-budget production.

With the Dhurandhar 2 clash now months behind it and the trailer finally public, the film enters its final promotional stretch — though Yash seems unfazed by the pressure. "When you want to do something in life, nothing should stop you," he said.
